sections.title: Objective type questions (2 parts of 1 mark, or 4 parts of ½ mark).

questions.q: Sati Pratha was practised in which a ____ woman was compelled to burn herself on the funeral ____ of her husband.
Fill in the blanks: The first Hindu Widow Remarriage Act was introduced in ____ owing to the relentless efforts of ____.
Fill in the blanks: The formation of the two ____ at Amritsar and Lahore in the 1870s was the beginning of the ____ reform movement among the Sikhs.
Complete the sentence: In September 1873 ____ Phule along with his followers formed the ____.
Match: (a) Ahmadiya Movement (b) Mohammedan Literary Society (c) Aligarh (M.A.O.) College (d) Hindu Widow Remarriage Act — (i) 1856 (ii) 1875 (iii) 1899 (iv) 1863

Fill in the blanks: (a) Annie Besant became the President of the ____ Society in 1907. (b) ____ established the Mukti Mission in Pune, a refuge for young widows who had been deserted and abused by their families.
Match: (a) Arya Mahila Samaj (b) Satya Shodhak Samaj (c) Ramakrishna Mission (d) Brahmo Samaj — (i) Raja Ram Mohan Roy (ii) Pandita Ramabai (iii) Jyotiba Phule (iv) Swami Vivekananda

Identify the person: (a) He and his wife Savitribai Phule are most known for their efforts to educate women, the lower castes and the masses. (b) He founded the Mohammadan Anglo-Oriental College at Aligarh.
questions.answer: (a) Jyotirao (Jyotiba) Phule (b) Sir Syed Ahmed Khan

questions.q: Answer briefly: (a) Why did Raja Ram Mohan Roy oppose Sati Pratha? (b) Why did Swami Dayanand Saraswati found the Arya Samaj?
questions.answer: (a) He was moved by his brother's widow being forced to commit sati; it was inhuman and, as he showed from the scriptures, had no sanction in Hindu religion. (b) To reform Hindu religion on the basis of the Vedas and to fight superstition, untouchability and caste rigidity in North India.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Describe any two endeavours of Raja Rammohan Roy in the field of social reform.
questions.answer: (1) He campaigned against sati, citing scriptures to show it had no religious sanction; with Lord Bentinck's support it was banned in 1829. (2) He advocated widow remarriage, opposed child marriage and idol worship, and promoted English and scientific education (English school in Calcutta, Hindu College).

or.q: Explain any two endeavours of Jyotirao Govindrao Phule.
or.answer: (1) He and Savitribai Phule opened schools for girls (1848, and in Poona in 1851) and educated women and lower castes. (2) In 1873 he founded the Satya Shodhak Samaj to free the lower castes from exploitation; he also promoted widow remarriage.

questions.q: Mention any two reforms brought by Swami Dayanand Saraswati in the field of education.
questions.answer: (1) He preached in Hindi so that ideas reached ordinary people of North India. (2) His followers started the D.A.V. (Dayanand Anglo-Vedic) schools and colleges which taught English and modern science along with Sanskrit and Vedic learning.

questions.q: Who founded the Brahmo Samaj? Mention any two of its principles.
questions.answer: Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded it in 1828. Principles: (1) worship of one God (monotheism) and opposition to idol worship and meaningless rituals; (2) unity of all religions and opposition to social evils like sati and child marriage.

questions.q: Why did reformers feel that social reform had no meaning without religious reform?
questions.answer: Most evil social practices like sati, untouchability and child marriage were followed in the name of religion and supported by priests. So reformers first showed from the scriptures that these practices had no religious sanction, and then tried to change society.

questions.q: Write any two limitations of the reform movements.
questions.answer: (1) They affected only a small percentage of the population, mostly the educated class. (2) They could not reach the vast masses of peasants and the urban poor, who continued to live in the same conditions.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Who introduced English education among the Muslims? Explain his contribution in this area.
questions.answer: Sir Syed Ahmed Khan. (1) He believed only modern Western education could bring Muslims progress and advocated English despite orthodox opposition. (2) He opened an English school at Ghazipur (1864) and founded the M.A.O. College at Aligarh (1875), which became Aligarh Muslim University. (3) He set up a scientific society to translate English books, published a journal and started the Mohammadan Educational Conference — the Aligarh Movement.

questions.q: Explain the contribution of Swami Dayanand Saraswati in reforming Hindu religion in India.
questions.answer: He founded the Arya Samaj in 1875, held the Vedas infallible and rejected ideas against them, wrote Satyarth Prakash and started the Shuddhi movement. He opposed idol worship, untouchability and caste rigidity, worked to improve women's condition, used Hindi to reach the people and inspired the D.A.V. schools; the Arya Samaj also built self-respect and self-reliance that helped the national movement.

questions.q: Explain the contribution of Swami Vivekananda in the religious and social reform movement in India.
questions.answer: He spread the teachings of Ramakrishna Paramhansa about the unity of religions and founded the Ramakrishna Mission. He stressed that Indians needed both spiritual and secular knowledge and faith in themselves. He fought superstition, caste rigidity and untouchability, worked for women's upliftment and education, and gave primary importance to removing ignorance.

questions.q: Explain the contribution of Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar in the field of education.
questions.answer: (1) He helped open about 35 girls' schools in Bengal and was a champion of women's education. (2) He encouraged the study of Sanskrit and Bengali literature and introduced Western thought in the Sanskrit College. (3) He got non-Brahmin students admitted to the Sanskrit College. He also campaigned for widow remarriage, leading to the 1856 Act.

questions.q: Why was Jyotirao Govindrao Phule considered an eminent reformer?
questions.answer: (1) He fought for equal rights for peasants and lower castes. (2) With Savitribai Phule he started schools for girls and educated women and the masses. (3) He promoted widow remarriage. (4) He founded the Satya Shodhak Samaj (1873) to protect lower castes from exploitation and atrocities.

questions.q: Describe the impact of the social and religious reform movements on Indian society.
questions.answer: (1) They spread a rational, scientific and humanitarian outlook and criticised caste and untouchability. (2) Laws were passed against sati and infanticide, for widow remarriage (1856) and inter-caste marriage (1872), and against child marriage (1929); women's education spread. (3) They gave Indians self-respect, self-confidence and pride in their country, creating national consciousness that led to the united freedom struggle.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: How did the socio-religious reform movements lead to the Indian National Movement? Explain in six points.
questions.answer: (1) They gave Indians self-respect, self-confidence and pride in their culture and country. (2) They spread rational and scientific thinking and modern education, producing an educated class aware of liberty and equality. (3) By attacking caste, untouchability and religious divisions they promoted social unity. (4) Better status and education brought women into public life and the freedom struggle (Sarojini Naidu, Aruna Asaf Ali, Laxmi Sehgal). (5) Organisations like the Arya Samaj and Theosophical Society built self-reliance and political awakening. (6) People became conscious of their identity as Indians, which led to a united struggle against the British; after 1919 the national movement itself carried forward social reform.

or.q: Who introduced English education among the Muslims? Explain in six points his contribution.
or.answer: Sir Syed Ahmed Khan. (1) He believed Muslims could progress only through modern Western scientific knowledge. (2) He advocated learning English despite opposition from orthodox Muslims. (3) He opened an English school at Ghazipur in 1864. (4) He founded the M.A.O. College at Aligarh in 1875, teaching humanities and science through English; it became Aligarh Muslim University. (5) He set up a scientific society to translate English books and published a journal for reform. (6) He started the Mohammadan Educational Conference and worked for women's education against purdah and polygamy — the Aligarh Movement.

questions.q: Explain the social practices that existed in 19th-century India and how reformers fought them.
questions.answer: (1) Female infanticide was common; it was later made illegal. (2) Child marriage was widespread; reformers opposed it and the Sharda Act (1929) fixed minimum ages. (3) Sati: Raja Ram Mohan Roy campaigned and it was banned in 1829. (4) Widows lived miserable lives; Vidyasagar's efforts produced the Widow Remarriage Act (1856), and Pandita Ramabai's Mukti Mission sheltered them. (5) Polygamy and purdah were opposed by Vidyasagar and Sir Syed. (6) Rigid caste and untouchability were attacked by the Arya Samaj, Phule's Satya Shodhak Samaj, Vivekananda and others; education, especially for girls, was the main tool of change.
